query: Across Type of Traveller and Class, which review themes are associated with higher vs. lower Overall Rating?

per_column.name: theme_crew_service
per_column.rationale: Binary presence flag for a crew/service theme; directly supports theme-vs-rating analysis. Samples confirm sound reading (crew praise=1, seat-only complaint=0). Partial topical overlap with the existing 'Staff Service' rating but the text-mention signal is a distinct axis.

per_column.name: theme_seat_comfort
per_column.rationale: Flags seat/comfort discussion. Well grounded across samples (legroom, narrow padding, comfortable seat all -> 1; unrelated review -> 0). Some redundancy with the original 'Seat Comfort' numeric rating, but captures whether the topic was raised in free text.

per_column.name: theme_food_quality
per_column.rationale: Food-theme flag; clean extraction in all samples (delicious/plentiful/available -> 1, silent rows -> 0). Useful grouping axis for the query despite overlap with 'Food & Beverages' rating.

per_column.name: theme_entertainment
per_column.rationale: IFE-theme flag; mostly grounded (IFE variety, dreadful sound, movies -> 1). Sample 4 (truncated text with no clear entertainment mention) was set to 1, a mild over-assertion, but overall sound.

per_column.name: theme_punctuality
per_column.rationale: Adds a genuine new axis (no equivalent original column). However sample 1 fires punctuality=1 with no timeliness/delay language in the text, an unsupported assertion, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: theme_value_money
per_column.rationale: Value-for-money theme flag; samples all 0 and consistent with texts that do not discuss price/value. Overlaps with existing 'Value For Money' rating but reflects a text-mention signal.

per_column.name: theme_cleanliness
per_column.rationale: New axis with no original counterpart. Well grounded (sanitized seat/clean bathroom -> 1; well-maintained cabin -> reasonable; silent rows -> 0).

per_column.name: theme_boarding
per_column.rationale: Boarding is a useful new theme, but the flag fires spuriously: samples 1 and 3 are set to 1 despite no boarding/gate/embarkation language in the source text. This confident over-assertion materially undermines groundedness.

per_column.name: review_sentiment_score
per_column.rationale: Continuous sentiment is somewhat more useful than a bare positive/negative flag and can help relate tone to rating, though it partly restates Overall Rating/Recommended. Sample values (positive reviews ~0.75-1.0, all-negative review -1.0) are sound readings of the text.

per_column.name: review_word_count
per_column.rationale: Raw word count is explicitly a generic length feature that gives no analytical leverage for associating themes with rating across segments. It is mechanically derivable from the text (well grounded) but adds little value here.

per_column.name: traveller_class_segment
per_column.rationale: Concatenation of Type of Traveller and Class -- exactly the grouping key the query calls for ('Across Type of Traveller and Class'). Values match the two source columns; deterministic and correct.

per_column.name: segment_mean_rating
per_column.rationale: Per-segment mean of Overall Rating; provides a baseline for comparing segments and is derivable from the table. Somewhat restates the segment key, but supports higher-vs-lower rating comparison.

per_column.name: rating_vs_segment_mean
per_column.rationale: Row-level deviation of Overall Rating from its segment mean -- a normalized signal directly useful for seeing which themes accompany above/below-average ratings within a segment. Reconstructed Overall Ratings from the samples are internally consistent (e.g. mean 7.29 + 1.71 = 9, matching the '9/10' review).

judge.rationale: The added set is well aligned with the query: theme flags supply the 'review themes' axis, traveller_class_segment supplies the exact grouping key, and segment_mean_rating / rating_vs_segment_mean give normalized rating comparisons -- a strong analytical toolkit. Usefulness is dragged down modestly by review_word_count (generic length feature) and partial redundancy of several theme flags with existing numeric sub-ratings and of the sentiment score with Overall Rating. Groundedness is generally strong: theme extractions, sentiment, the segment key, and the rating-deviation arithmetic all check out against the sample texts. It is reduced by two themes that fire without textual support -- theme_boarding (spurious 1s in samples 1 and 3) and theme_punctuality (spurious 1 in sample 1) -- indicating some over-assertion in the noisier theme detectors.
